work.title: The Third Part of King Henry the Sixth
work.author: William Shakespeare

scene.label: Act 2, Scene 6
scene.title: SCENE VI. Another Part of the Field

content.text: A loud alarum. Enter Clifford, wounded.

lines.text: Here burns my candle out; ay, here it dies,
lines.plainText: Here burns my candle out ay here it dies

lines.text: Which whiles it lasted gave King Henry light.
lines.plainText: Which whiles it lasted gave King Henry light

lines.text: O Lancaster, I fear thy overthrow
lines.plainText: O Lancaster I fear thy overthrow

lines.text: More than my body's parting with my soul!
lines.plainText: More than my body's parting with my soul

lines.text: My love and fear glued many friends to thee;
lines.plainText: My love and fear glued many friends to thee

lines.text: And, now I fall, thy tough commixtures melts,
lines.plainText: And now I fall thy tough commixtures melts

lines.text: Impairing Henry, strengthening misproud York.
lines.plainText: Impairing Henry strengthening misproud York

lines.text: The common people swarm like summer flies;
lines.plainText: The common people swarm like summer flies

lines.text: And whither fly the gnats but to the sun?
lines.plainText: And whither fly the gnats but to the sun

lines.text: And who shines now but Henry's enemies?
lines.plainText: And who shines now but Henry's enemies

lines.text: O Phoebus, hadst thou never given consent
lines.plainText: O Phoebus hadst thou never given consent

lines.text: That Phaëthon should check thy fiery steeds,
lines.plainText: That Phathon should check thy fiery steeds

lines.text: Thy burning car never had scorched the earth!
lines.plainText: Thy burning car never had scorched the earth

lines.text: And, Henry, hadst thou swayed as kings should do,
lines.plainText: And Henry hadst thou swayed as kings should do

lines.text: Or as thy father and his father did,
lines.plainText: Or as thy father and his father did

lines.text: Giving no ground unto the house of York,
lines.plainText: Giving no ground unto the house of York

lines.text: They never then had sprung like summer flies;
lines.plainText: They never then had sprung like summer flies

lines.text: I, and ten thousand in this luckless realm
lines.plainText: I and ten thousand in this luckless realm

lines.text: Had left no mourning widows for our death,
lines.plainText: Had left no mourning widows for our death

lines.text: And thou this day hadst kept thy chair in peace.
lines.plainText: And thou this day hadst kept thy chair in peace

lines.text: For what doth cherish weeds but gentle air?
lines.plainText: For what doth cherish weeds but gentle air

lines.text: And what makes robbers bold but too much lenity?
lines.plainText: And what makes robbers bold but too much lenity

lines.text: Bootless are plaints, and cureless are my wounds;
lines.plainText: Bootless are plaints and cureless are my wounds

lines.text: No way to fly, nor strength to hold out flight.
lines.plainText: No way to fly nor strength to hold out flight

lines.text: The foe is merciless and will not pity,
lines.plainText: The foe is merciless and will not pity

lines.text: For at their hands I have deserved no pity.
lines.plainText: For at their hands I have deserved no pity

lines.text: The air hath got into my deadly wounds,
lines.plainText: The air hath got into my deadly wounds

lines.text: And much effuse of blood doth make me faint.
lines.plainText: And much effuse of blood doth make me faint

lines.text: Come, York and Richard, Warwick, and the rest;
lines.plainText: Come York and Richard Warwick and the rest

lines.text: I stabbed your fathers' bosoms, split my breast.
lines.plainText: I stabbed your fathers' bosoms split my breast

content.text: Alarum and retreat. Enter Edward, George, Richard, Montague, Warwick and Soldiers.

lines.text: Now breathe we, lords. Good fortune bids us pause
lines.plainText: Now breathe we lords Good fortune bids us pause

lines.text: And smooth the frowns of war with peaceful looks.
lines.plainText: And smooth the frowns of war with peaceful looks

lines.text: Some troops pursue the bloody-minded Queen
lines.plainText: Some troops pursue the bloodyminded Queen

lines.text: That led calm Henry, though he were a king,
lines.plainText: That led calm Henry though he were a king

lines.text: As doth a sail, filled with a fretting gust,
lines.plainText: As doth a sail filled with a fretting gust

lines.text: Command an argosy to stem the waves.
lines.plainText: Command an argosy to stem the waves

lines.text: But think you, lords, that Clifford fled with them?
lines.plainText: But think you lords that Clifford fled with them

lines.text: No, 'tis impossible he should escape;
lines.plainText: No 'tis impossible he should escape

lines.text: For, though before his face I speak the words,
lines.plainText: For though before his face I speak the words

lines.text: Your brother Richard marked him for the grave,
lines.plainText: Your brother Richard marked him for the grave

lines.text: And whereso'er he is, he's surely dead.
lines.plainText: And whereso'er he is he's surely dead

lines.text: Whose soul is that which takes her heavy leave?
lines.plainText: Whose soul is that which takes her heavy leave

lines.text: A deadly groan, like life and death's departing.
lines.plainText: A deadly groan like life and death's departing

lines.text: See who it is; and, now the battle's ended,
lines.plainText: See who it is and now the battle's ended

lines.text: If friend or foe, let him be gently used.
lines.plainText: If friend or foe let him be gently used

lines.text: Revoke that doom of mercy, for 'tis Clifford,
lines.plainText: Revoke that doom of mercy for 'tis Clifford

lines.text: Who, not contented that he lopped the branch
lines.plainText: Who not contented that he lopped the branch

lines.text: In hewing Rutland when his leaves put forth,
lines.plainText: In hewing Rutland when his leaves put forth

lines.text: But set his murdering knife unto the root
lines.plainText: But set his murdering knife unto the root

lines.text: From whence that tender spray did sweetly spring,
lines.plainText: From whence that tender spray did sweetly spring

lines.text: I mean our princely father, Duke of York.
lines.plainText: I mean our princely father Duke of York

lines.text: From off the gates of York fetch down the head,
lines.plainText: From off the gates of York fetch down the head

lines.text: Your father's head, which Clifford placed there;
lines.plainText: Your father's head which Clifford placed there

lines.text: Instead whereof let this supply the room.
lines.plainText: Instead whereof let this supply the room

lines.text: Measure for measure must be answered.
lines.plainText: Measure for measure must be answered

lines.text: Bring forth that fatal screech-owl to our house,
lines.plainText: Bring forth that fatal screechowl to our house

lines.text: That nothing sung but death to us and ours;
lines.plainText: That nothing sung but death to us and ours

lines.text: Now death shall stop his dismal threatening sound,
lines.plainText: Now death shall stop his dismal threatening sound

lines.text: And his ill-boding tongue no more shall speak.
lines.plainText: And his illboding tongue no more shall speak

lines.text: I think his understanding is bereft.
lines.plainText: I think his understanding is bereft

lines.text: Speak, Clifford, dost thou know who speaks to thee?
lines.plainText: Speak Clifford dost thou know who speaks to thee

lines.text: Dark cloudy death o'ershades his beams of life,
lines.plainText: Dark cloudy death o'ershades his beams of life

lines.text: And he nor sees nor hears us, what we say.
lines.plainText: And he nor sees nor hears us what we say

lines.text: O, would he did, and so, perhaps, he doth!
lines.plainText: O would he did and so perhaps he doth

lines.text: 'Tis but his policy to counterfeit,
lines.plainText: 'Tis but his policy to counterfeit

lines.text: Because he would avoid such bitter taunts
lines.plainText: Because he would avoid such bitter taunts

lines.text: Which in the time of death he gave our father.
lines.plainText: Which in the time of death he gave our father

lines.text: If so thou think'st, vex him with eager words.
lines.plainText: If so thou think'st vex him with eager words

lines.text: Clifford, ask mercy, and obtain no grace.
lines.plainText: Clifford ask mercy and obtain no grace

lines.text: Clifford, repent in bootless penitence.
lines.plainText: Clifford repent in bootless penitence

lines.text: Clifford, devise excuses for thy faults.
lines.plainText: Clifford devise excuses for thy faults

lines.text: While we devise fell tortures for thy faults.
lines.plainText: While we devise fell tortures for thy faults

lines.text: Thou didst love York, and I am son to York.
lines.plainText: Thou didst love York and I am son to York

lines.text: Thou pitied'st Rutland, I will pity thee.
lines.plainText: Thou pitied'st Rutland I will pity thee

lines.text: Where's Captain Margaret to fence you now?
lines.plainText: Where's Captain Margaret to fence you now

lines.text: They mock thee, Clifford; swear as thou wast wont.
lines.plainText: They mock thee Clifford swear as thou wast wont

lines.text: What, not an oath? Nay then, the world goes hard
lines.plainText: What not an oath Nay then the world goes hard

lines.text: When Clifford cannot spare his friends an oath.
lines.plainText: When Clifford cannot spare his friends an oath

lines.text: I know by that he's dead; and, by my soul,
lines.plainText: I know by that he's dead and by my soul

lines.text: If this right hand would buy but two hours' life,
lines.plainText: If this right hand would buy but two hours' life

lines.text: That I in all despite might rail at him,
lines.plainText: That I in all despite might rail at him

lines.text: This hand should chop it off, and with the issuing blood
lines.plainText: This hand should chop it off and with the issuing blood

lines.text: Stifle the villain whose unstaunched thirst
lines.plainText: Stifle the villain whose unstaunched thirst

lines.text: York and young Rutland could not satisfy.
lines.plainText: York and young Rutland could not satisfy

lines.text: Ay, but he's dead. Off with the traitor's head,
lines.plainText: Ay but he's dead Off with the traitor's head

lines.text: And rear it in the place your father's stands.
lines.plainText: And rear it in the place your father's stands

lines.text: And now to London with triumphant march,
lines.plainText: And now to London with triumphant march

lines.text: There to be crowned England's royal king;
lines.plainText: There to be crowned England's royal king

lines.text: From whence shall Warwick cut the sea to France,
lines.plainText: From whence shall Warwick cut the sea to France

lines.text: And ask the Lady Bona for thy queen.
lines.plainText: And ask the Lady Bona for thy queen

lines.text: So shalt thou sinew both these lands together,
lines.plainText: So shalt thou sinew both these lands together

lines.text: And, having France thy friend, thou shalt not dread
lines.plainText: And having France thy friend thou shalt not dread

lines.text: The scattered foe that hopes to rise again;
lines.plainText: The scattered foe that hopes to rise again

lines.text: For though they cannot greatly sting to hurt,
lines.plainText: For though they cannot greatly sting to hurt

lines.text: Yet look to have them buzz to offend thine ears.
lines.plainText: Yet look to have them buzz to offend thine ears

lines.text: First will I see the coronation,
lines.plainText: First will I see the coronation

lines.text: And then to Brittany I'll cross the sea
lines.plainText: And then to Brittany I'll cross the sea

lines.text: To effect this marriage, so it please my lord.
lines.plainText: To effect this marriage so it please my lord

lines.text: Even as thou wilt, sweet Warwick, let it be;
lines.plainText: Even as thou wilt sweet Warwick let it be

lines.text: For in thy shoulder do I build my seat,
lines.plainText: For in thy shoulder do I build my seat

lines.text: And never will I undertake the thing
lines.plainText: And never will I undertake the thing

lines.text: Wherein thy counsel and consent is wanting.
lines.plainText: Wherein thy counsel and consent is wanting

lines.text: Richard, I will create thee Duke of Gloucester;
lines.plainText: Richard I will create thee Duke of Gloucester

lines.text: And George, of Clarence. Warwick, as ourself,
lines.plainText: And George of Clarence Warwick as ourself

lines.text: Shall do and undo as him pleaseth best.
lines.plainText: Shall do and undo as him pleaseth best

lines.text: Let me be Duke of Clarence, George of Gloucester,
lines.plainText: Let me be Duke of Clarence George of Gloucester

lines.text: For Gloucester's dukedom is too ominous.
lines.plainText: For Gloucester's dukedom is too ominous

lines.text: Tut, that's a foolish observation.
lines.plainText: Tut that's a foolish observation

lines.text: Richard, be Duke of Gloucester. Now to London,
lines.plainText: Richard be Duke of Gloucester Now to London

lines.text: To see these honours in possession.
lines.plainText: To see these honours in possession
